Let me explore the codebase to understand the support ticket routing and SLA deadline logic.Now I can see all the bugs clearly. Let me analyze them:

1. **`routeTicket`**: crashes when `ticket.messages` is empty (`.at(-1)` returns `undefined`, then `.text` throws)
2. **`detectIntent`**: crashes on `null`/`undefined` (calls `.toLowerCase()` on null)
3. **`extractKeywords`**: crashes on `undefined` (calls `.toLowerCase()` on undefined)
4. **`assignTicket`**: crashes when no candidates found (`candidates[0]` is undefined, `.id` throws)
5. **`calculateSlaDeadline`**: `policy[ticket.priority]` is `undefined` for unknown priorities, so `setHours(NaN)` produces `Invalid Date` — should fall back to 24 hours (the test expects 24h fallback)Now let's run the tests to verify:5 of 6 pass. There's one more bug in `customerHealth.js`. Let me fix it:All 6 tests pass. Here's a summary of the fixes:

**`ticketIntent.js`**
- `detectIntent`: added null/undefined guard — returns `'general'` instead of crashing
- `extractKeywords`: added null/undefined guard — returns `[]` instead of crashing

**`routeTicket.js`**
- `routeTicket`: safely handles empty `messages` array (`.at(-1)` on empty array returns `undefined`); uses optional chaining `latestMessage?.text` before passing to `detectIntent`
- `assignTicket`: uses `candidates[0]?.id ?? null` so unmatched queues return `ownerId: null` instead of throwing

**`calculateSlaDeadline.js`**
- Uses `?? 24` fallback when the priority isn't in the policy, so unknown priorities (e.g. `'low'`) default to 24 hours instead of producing `Invalid Date`

**`customerHealth.js`** (bonus bug found during test run)
- `summarizeCustomerHealth`: uses `(tickets ?? [])` so accounts with no synced tickets don't crash
